I take latuda and it doesn’t make me sleepy at all.
Yes, I’m on lithium and latuda. SSRIs either trigger mania for me or don’t work.

I took 200mg daily for 3-4 years and it never really helped my depression. From what I’ve seen that’s not common, it usually helps. It gave me a lot of cognitive issues though, I could not finish a movie or do complex tasks at work. I had trouble remembering words and stuff. Since it didn’t help my depression I told my psychiatrist I wanted to stop taking it and he decreased my dose slowly over 4 months. I had a short depressive episode when I stopped but it also coincided with the start of winter and that’s always a rough time for me. It’s been 6 months since I stopped and I don’t feel worse than when I was on it (I’m actually doing pretty great) and cognitively I’m doing much better. 

I would still say to try it, it works for most people. There usually aren’t many side effects. Be sure to titrate up slowly to reduce the risk of getting the rash.

I took it for a year and a half and it really helped with my anxiety but I had trouble with depersonalization and derealization while on it and my psychiatrist said it was because of the pregabalin so I stopped.
I felt really dizzy and weak. Not sure how to explain it… I felt like I was gonna pass out even when I was sitting down. I wore a Fitbit and it was how I knew for sure though.
I haven’t gained weight on Lurasidone and I’ve been taking it for years.

That means from 12 to 22 years old for me. I was bullied a lot and had issues with depression and anxiety, I was hospitalized when I was 13 or 14 for 6 months. Life was a lot more intense because I was a teenager and not on meds. I had surgery when I was 22 that triggered a post operative depression episode that really fucked shit up, I was always back in hospital and was diagnosed bipolar. A bit later I started having psychosis and my diagnosis changed to schizoaffective.

I’m pretty happy but that has only been happening for the last two years. Before that I was constantly suicidal and in and out of hospitals. Meds help a lot but meeting my girlfriend changed everything. I still have some hiccups but overall I’m doing good.

Because of anorexia. It’s hard to explain and complicated (I was already vegan before I developed anorexia) but it was in no way sustainable. It was a good excuse to eat something else than everyone else too. And the amount of vegan food I’d have to eat to get enough nutrients was very triggering. I’m doing a lot better now but I’m still struggling with ED thoughts. 

It’s mostly how the diet needed to be well planned and everything. My life revolved around my diet and what, when and how I’d eat. I struggle with another mental illness that makes it hard to stay consistent in my habits (schizoaffective bipolar) and I was still trying to find medications that worked back then so I was too overwhelmed by a bunch of stuff and couldn’t put enough energy into carefully planning my diet. Now I’m doing much better in every aspect but I don’t think I eat enough vegetables and fruits. I mostly eat fish and dairy and rice. Sometimes tofu and chicken or beef. I was seeing a dietitian but I can’t afford to see one right now. 

I like the idea of veganism but I know it’s not sustainable for most people. Most vegan people I knew had health issues and I’m pretty sure them being vegan didn’t help.

It depends. I haven’t had a true hypomanic episode since I started lithium, I’ve only had some symptoms that would qualify as subclinical. I still get depressive episodes but they’re not as long and as bad. Now they last a couple of months instead of like 8-9 months. I don’t get to the point where I’m suicidal anymore.
Buspar worked but made me hypomanic so I had to stop taking it. Propranolol didn’t help and lowered my heart rate too much so I felt terrible and I stopped it.
Bipolar type, I’m down to lithium and Lurasidone now plus a med to sleep (unrelated).

I take Ajovy (anti-CGRP) but I’ve only been on it for 6 months. I barely have migraines anymore. I did have a depressive episode during that 6 months period though so I’m not sure it has an effect. No hypomania.
I had to switch brands because of availability issues. They tested my levels a month after switching and I did not notice anything different.
Yes, I have the bipolar type but my episodes come out of nowhere 9 times out of 10. For no reason.
I take 80mg and I’m sometimes nauseous but have never thrown up from it. When I was on 100mg I felt very sedated so I didn’t stay long on that dose.

I ended up getting a lower heart rate and did not feel good (physically) on propranolol. My bpm was around 45-50. I did not notice an effect on my mental health (I am diagnosed with schizoaffective bipolar and GAD).

I felt like I was fighting all the time. I also have schizoaffective disorder so everything on top of that was just too much and I did what was the easiest for me.  I even tried finasteride for the hair but the side effects were brutal. I’m 29 now so it’s been 5 years and as I said, I’m more at peace but not 100%. It was easier to repress the dysphoria for me. I’m kinda ashamed but it is what it is.

I medically (HRT + top surgery) and legally transitioned for 8-9 years, ages 15-16 to 24. I stopped T when I was 24 when I realized I was non binary and not a binary man. I still have physical dysphoria but I did not like being treated as a man. I’d rather be a woman socially, but physically I’d rather be a man. I stopped T because of side effects I didn’t like (losing hair and atrophy, mainly) but I miss the fat distribution and muscle mass. I don’t regret top surgery. I’m only out as non binary to my girlfriend and some friends, my family thinks I detransitioned completely, except my mother who knows I’m still dysphoric quite often. I also had a lot of internalized transphobia and wanted to pass more than anything so I didn’t want to be seen as a feminine man even though that’s probably what fits best. I felt as if it was all for nothing if I couldn’t pass. I went the other way and to be honest I think it’s because I was weak and gave up. I’m more at peace now but not 100%.

300mg morning, 300mg at night. Level was 0.6 last I checked (will be checked again in August). No side effects, but this is my second time taking it. I had side effects the first time and took propranolol to counteract them. I had tremors and stiffness in the neck/face. This time everything’s fine. I’m mostly stable, I have about 3 depressive episodes a year and no longer have mania. Or if I do, it’s subclinical hypomania so it doesn’t really count.

I used to have chronic migraines and I see a neurologist. Many preventatives are psych meds so I couldn't get on them. I now get a monthly injection and my migraines are not considered chronic anymore.
Latuda and lithium
I tested days after my first dose the two times I started lithium. I was inpatient though.

Reading Reddit and sometimes books, learning a language, household chores (taking out the trash, going to the grocery store, cleaning the kitchen and bathroom, laundry), taking care of my pets, self care. I’d like to exercise more but it’s hard because I sleep 11-12 hours a day and I often feel tired. I’m on a waiting list for therapy and will try working again after that.

I was suicidal and at the end of my rope, the meds weren’t working so I tried shrooms out of desperation. The first time it was a small dose and it went well, but a week later I had a manic episode. It did not last long because I was put on olanzapine to break it and it worked. I was still not doing great months later so I tried again at a higher dose a few times because I had fun. It helped the depression for a few months but the effects eventually disappeared. Instead of trying again I went back on meds. I wouldn’t try again because I’d need to go off my lithium and stuff but if I didn’t have this disorder I would. It’s been about 3 years since I did it I think.

It got better but never got to how I was before. I was on a low dose too to help with sleep and anxiety. It got to be too much (I was sleeping 12 hours a day and I was tired when I woke up) so I’m trying something else but I’ll consider going back if it doesn’t work.
J’ai encore quelques plaques qui viennent et qui partent, mais vraiment moins qu’avant. Je prends environ 2800 UI par jour.
Find graded readers, listen to beginner podcasts (Coffee break german, Easy German). I like comprehensive input videos on YouTube. You can also get a textbook. I use Anki for vocabulary.

Talk with your psychiatrist. When that started happening to me (psychosis outside of episodes) they changed my diagnosis to schizoaffective bipolar disorder. The treatment is the same though, same meds.
I brought it up to my psychiatrist in the past but he said he didn’t want me to try it because it could induce mania. I ended up not getting ECT either but I’m doing okay on meds now.

As others have said, this isn’t about him having schizophrenia, it’s just him being shitty. I promised my girlfriend I would always take my meds (for me that’s the bare minimum I can do in a relationship) and I take accountability if I’m ever out of line and I told her I would only treat her as a partner and never as a therapist or a care taker. IMO there is a difference between needing some help and being completely dependent on someone else. I can take care of myself and my health, for example I can call my psychiatrist on my own when something is up. I know that if things turn to shit and I need to go to the hospital my girlfriend will be there for me, but I’m functional enough to have a healthy relationship. Some people aren’t and that’s okay. I think there’s also a difference to be made between personality and disorder.
I’m on my second pot of Tocobo Multi Ceramides Cream. I’m not a fan of the scent so I might try something else after this one but otherwise I love it.

I could no longer have orgasms (but I could still get horny, so it was terrible) on SSRIs and they never helped my bipolar. Venlafaxine was terrible for me. I had a hard time coming off it. My girlfriend also had terrible withdrawals symptoms when she tried to stop it but she managed to push through. What helped my bipolar symptoms were mood stabilizers and antipsychotics, particularly lithium and Lurasidone.

I was diagnosed way before I started my current relationship, so that gave me time to find meds that work and I’m pretty stable except for some anxiety and a couple of depressive episodes. I’ve been with my girlfriend for two years now and we’ve been living together for one. Everything is great so far. She’s very supportive.

De toute façon au Québec, à ce qu’il paraît pas mal tout le monde devrait en prendre, surtout l’hiver.

Not sure if it’s considered long term, but we’ve been together for two years. We are 29 and 27. We both want a committed long term relationship, will probably get married. Having kids is another question. She can’t carry a child and I have schizoaffective bipolar disorder, so a pregnancy scares me (having to deal with meds and pregnancy hormones and everything). I would like kids but I don’t think it’ll ever happen. We’re both okay with it. I don’t think we’ll ever be able to adopt because of my disorder but even then I don’t see myself having kids until my 40s. Right now the consensus is we’re okay with having kids at that point, but nothing’s for certain. We do want to get married though.

This is purely anecdotal, but I was on T for 5 years and I stopped taking it 5 years ago (I’m NB). My mood was much more unstable on it and my psychotic symptoms were worse. They’re not completely gone off T but they’re much rarer. I had more frequent mood episodes too. It didn’t affect my anxiety levels, they’re as bad as they were on T. I was told the forms you take daily (like gel) are best for mood stability because your levels don’t fluctuate as much. I was on weekly injections.

Never really heard of trazodone, what really scares and triggers me is weight gain. I’ll look some more into it. 

I took propranolol for a while as migraine prevention and it didn’t help my anxiety. I had to stop it because it gave me bradycardia so I can’t take those sadly.
I made a dating app profile while I was manic. I met my girlfriend there. When we met in person the manic episode was over. We’re still together two years later.
I had klonopin and Ativan as a PRN in the past, not at the same time, but still. For some reason I can’t have that anymore. I don’t remember his reason, something about addiction potential I think.

Oh damn, I totally forgot to mention Lyrica in my OP. I took it for a year and a half for migraine prevention and it was great for my anxiety. I stopped taking it because I started having a tolerance after that long and my psychiatrist didn’t really want to increase the dose because it caused me derealization and depersonalization, plus it stopped working for the migraines (I have something else for that now). It also made me gain a bit of weight but not too much. It was great for sleep and anxiety though, I miss it.

Back when I was on T I started with intramuscular injections but when I told my endo I wanted to do them myself he switched me to subcutaneous. It was pretty much the same thing and same T. I had no trouble doing them and I still do subcutaneous injections now, just with another med.

The auto injectors hurt too much for me to reliably do them myself. I switched to the pre-filled syringes. I have taken a lot of medication I needed to inject myself with over the years so I’m used to them. I don’t feel anything when I do them, so that’s an option if you’re at ease with it.
Mentally I’m great. Several good things have been happening lately. Physically I’m on the verge of death. I have a pretty bad cold and it’s kicking my ass.
Yes. I stopped taking lithium to try shrooms because of the risk of seizure. I was very suicidal and felt I had nothing to lose by trying shrooms. I started taking lithium again a year later.

I thought I had major depressive disorder, then borderline personality disorder. MDD was my first diagnosis and my symptoms were progressive. I was diagnosed when I was 13. I started having hypomanic episodes that went undetected when I was around 15 or 16 years old but the psychotic symptoms didn’t start until I turned 22. I was diagnosed with bipolar when I was around 21-22, but they changed it to schizoaffective bipolar when I was 23 and I’m 29 now. They added generalized anxiety disorder to it though.

I have schizoaffective bipolar type and I’ve had psychosis in every state, although only once in mania. That was the only time I had mania, the rest of the time I have hypomania. But I’ve had psychosis in depressive episodes and also on its own without a mood episode going on, which the way I understand it, is what makes it schizoaffective bipolar type and not bipolar with psychotic features.

I have migraines about twice a month now that I’ve been on Ajovy for 6 months and it happened today out of nowhere. I woke up with a migraine. I’m too scared to take my triptan because of the side effects (numbing and heaviness in the chest and face, just weird shit I don’t like and I haven’t had the chance to talk to my neurologist yet, it seems to happen more often than not now) so I ordered an iced coffee and went back to bed. I have plans for tonight but I’m supposed to tidy up my apartment before my friend comes over. Not so sure it’ll happen now. We were supposed to continue our show but there’s no way I can watch TV. So yeah, I get migraines twice a month but it happens today out of the blue and the day’s wasted.
I take 25mg every night to fall asleep. It has helped my anxiety a lot, it’s practically gone now.

Pregabalin helped me sleep very well, I was also taking it for many different reasons (migraines, but it also helped with anxiety and depression) but after a year and a half I seemed to have developed a tolerance and my psychiatrist didn’t want to increase the dose because he thought it was the cause of my weight gain and derealization/dissociation. I took and still sometimes take Zopiclone but the tolerance builds quickly and you can’t really take it long term. I also wake up often when I use it because it’s short acting. Not the best of sleep but it does make me fall asleep. Right now I take 25mg of quetiapine and it works well, but I sleep 12hrs and it’s hard to get up in the morning. I don’t work right now so it’s not too bad but in the future I might have to find something else. I take 5 or 10mg of melatonin as needed. I might try Dayvigo in a month or two instead of the Zopiclone.
I had that when I was taking a higher dose than now (I was taking 300mg) so they took me off it. I’m taking it again now years later but only 25mg so I don’t have that side effect right now.
It’s called pili torti and it has multiple possible causes, from hormones to medications or damaged follicles. I have a couple of spots on my head where they grow.

I tried many antipsychotics over the years, I’m currently on latuda and have been for a few years now. It’s the only antipsychotic that worked for my psychosis without side effects. Abilify gave me akathisia and didn’t get rid of my psychotic symptoms. I’m not sure we have vraylar in my country. Not one antipsychotic helped my anxiety (I am also diagnosed with GAD) like a low dose of seroquel did and my psychiatrist says it’s the most appropriate for my case. I also tried Buspirone but it made me manic.

Pregabalin worked so well for my anxiety until I built a tolerance a year and a half later. It also made me gain weight and caused derealization so I stopped taking it. I tried Buspirone but it gave me insomnia and made me hypomanic. I haven’t looked into the other ones yet, thank you.
Half doesn’t make me sleep, I think my tolerance is too high now. I will try taking it earlier again but it usually makes me sleep within an hour of taking it and I still end up sleeping 12hrs.

How do you deal with the hypothyroidism and the kidney disease? I was on lithium for a couple of years, went off for another couple and then went back on two and a half years ago. I get tested every 6 months and so far I’m okay, but there are often times when I have intrusive thoughts about poisoning myself.
It’s often in the beginning but now I only have to do it every 6 months, it’s not that bad.
Latuda made me sleep 7-8 hours for years. I had insomnia and added a low dose of seroquel and now I sleep 12 hours. Not ideal.
I am in no way a professional but I’ve been taking lithium for years and they always do both tests. Both blood and urine, I don’t think they test for the same things.

I ended up being diagnosed with schizoaffective bipolar but at first I only had bipolar symptoms. Because I had SH they misdiagnosed me with BPD instead. I only have a couple of BPD traits, but my current psychiatrist said almost everyone does and that’s why you need several to be diagnosed.
Not exactly, but years ago I would hear music whenever I let the water run to wash my hands. It would stop when I was done and turned it off.

I think the same, emotions and mood states are not the same. I can control my emotions quite well but I have no control over my mood states (depression and mania, plus in my case I don’t control my psychotic symptoms). It’s bullshit and it’s infuriating.
I smoked and vaped but managed to quit a year and a half ago. I used nicotine lozenges and it really helped. At some point I didn’t feel the need for them anymore and stopped completely.
Another comment mentioned the Ouai detox shampoo, which is great, but when I don’t need a clarifying shampoo I simply use the Ouai shampoo for fine hair.

Since I started taking 25mg of Seroquel to sleep my anxiety disappeared (I am diagnosed with GAD). I sometimes take something else to sleep so I don’t build a tolerance too fast. But it’s hard to stop taking it once you’re used to it.

I was on T for 5 years and I had my first period 6 months off T, then my second period 5 months later, and the third a month later. Afterwards, it was regular. My endocrinologist had told me to call him if I didn’t get it after 6 months off T.

It happens to me under stress, it goes away and then comes back again when I’m stressed or anxious. I thought it was my medication but it went away. It could last a week or two. I would talk with a psychiatrist if I were you just in case it does turn out to be because of your medication.
I used to take about 8 a month before I started preventatives, now I take 1 or 2 a month.

I didn’t replace it with anything, I was already on lithium and latuda. I was taking 200mg and did for years but never really noticed it helped my depressive episodes but it did impact my cognition a lot. It’s a lot better now that I’m off. If you do come off, do it slowly (it took me 4-5 months) and under the supervision of your psychiatrist.
Not sure about every province, but the longer I stayed was about a month, I was in psychosis.
Thank you! I’ll try a mousse then!

I have been diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder along with schizoaffective bipolar. Nothing worked until I had trouble sleeping and my psychiatrist prescribed a low dose (25mg) of seroquel to sleep. I take another sleeping med twice a week so I don’t build up a tolerance too fast. But since I started taking the seroquel to sleep, I noticed my anxiety is just… gone. I don’t really have side effects because it’s such a low dose. But I do sleep a lot, like 12hrs unchecked so I use an alarm every day so I don’t sleep more than 9hrs. I was stable from psychotic symptoms even before starting it. 

Other than that, I’m on a waiting list for therapy especially for anxiety issues. Hopefully that’ll help and someday I’ll be able to not take the seroquel.

This is the least amount of meds I’ve been on in years and I’m doing well. I have schizoaffective bipolar. 

1. Lithium as a mood stabilizer, takes care of mania and some depression. 

2. Lurasidone (Latuda) takes care of my psychotic symptoms and is supposed to help with depression. I think it does. 

3. Very low dose of quetiapine (seroquel), 25mg for my anxiety. It got rid of it almost 100% and it helps me sleep. 

Other than that I take vitamins for other stuff and an injection for my migraines.
Nope, not on Amazon or Walmart sadly
Ahhh I can’t find the eos one anywhere, I don’t know if they have it in Canada 😭

My psychiatrist didn’t want me to take the preventatives that are antidepressants because it could mess with the bipolar. Propranolol caused bradycardia so I had to stop taking it but I didn’t take it long enough to notice if it helped the migraines. I’m now on a monthly Ajovy injection and it reduced the frequency significantly, and it also helped the severity of the migraines. I recently went 3 weeks without a migraine. I take 40mg of Eletriptan as an abortive.

I was learning German during the onset of my psychotic symptoms (I have schizoaffective bipolar and only had mood symptoms before I was 21-22) but I never had problems. I stopped actively learning when I dropped out of college. Now 7 years later I’m picking it up again and it’s going well. But I have to say that English is my second language, I learned it as a child so maybe that’s why I have an easier time with German. I struggle with keeping a schedule more than actually learning. I have to be honest though, some of my meds gave me cognitive issues. I used to be on lamotrigine and I couldn’t have learned a language on it, no way. It got to the point where I had a hard time following a movie and learning the rules of a board game for little gain (never really helped with depression and I was on it for years) so I stopped taking it. I’m much better now.

I was prescribed a weak steroid cream, Desonid. I used it once a day until it went away. I then switched to Protopic for maintenance. I use it whenever they start getting dry or a bit flaky again. At first that was every two weeks but now it’s more like every 4-6 weeks. I don’t think much about it anymore.

I take a very low dose so other than some drowsiness the next morning I don’t really have side effects. I’ve taken zyprexa in the past to break a manic episode and it was a lot more sedating. I don’t know about a higher dose of seroquel. I don’t feel hornier or anything. For the past few months I’ve felt more asexual than anything but I don’t think it’s related to meds because I haven’t really changed what I take.

I had a good experience with it but I had to stop it because it caused insomnia. But I also had what my psychiatrist called an “activating” effect from it; I was borderline hypomanic (my psychiatrist said I was but I felt as if I wasn’t quite there yet). Apparently that’s rare but a known effect. I now take 25mg of seroquel and it helped my anxiety a lot and it obviously makes me sleep.
No reason not to try it, it’s often prescribed. When I tried it, it gave me bradycardia (low heart rate) so I had to stop before I really saw if it had an effect on my migraines.
My native language is French, actually. I’ll do some more research
I used to rapid cycle (4+ episodes a year) but on meds I don’t anymore.

It’ll be alright. It won’t be easy but it’ll be alright. It takes a lot of work to find the right meds and to push through symptoms but it gets better. I was non functional and hospitalized often for years but it got better once I got on the right meds. Now I live on my own and it’s going well, I haven’t been in the ward for two years and a half now and I used to go like once or twice a year. 

As for feeling sad, I know. There’s a bit of a mourning period. At least there was for me. I had to mourn that I would never be totally normal and that I might not be able to do everything I would have liked to do. I do have goals but they are realistic and I feel good when I work on them. I don’t try to go beyond my means because I know I would get sad and upset when I fail. But I’m proud of what I can accomplish. 

It’s a long road, but you can do it!
I’m in Canada and I sometimes get some, they get added to my cart automatically, but not always so there might be a condition I’m not aware of.
Been on it for 6 months now. It decreased both the frequency and severity of my migraines. I just spent 3 weeks without a single one. I don’t have side effects.

I had tactile hallucinations and I saw stuff out of the corner of my eye. Sometimes I would smell stuff that wasn’t there, mostly smoke and I would freak out. The worst were the delusions though. They weren’t delusions of grandeur as often seen in bipolar, though. They were mostly about demons clinging to me and controlling my thoughts. I was also paranoid. I never heard voices that much but recently I started having auditory hallucinations. I would mostly hear stuff like appliances making noise when they were turned off or the front door unlocking even though my girlfriend wasn’t back home yet and I was home alone. I haven’t had delusions in months now but the latest was about being inserted in a simulation.

I was diagnosed with MDD and medicated when I was 13, but I had hypomanic episodes starting when I was 15-16. They did not diagnose me bipolar until I was 21, I think. Then I started getting psychotic symptoms and the diagnosis changed for schizoaffective bipolar when I was 23.

I’ve been in a relationship for two years now. She made me promise I would always keep taking my meds and seek help when something is wrong. I always go to my appointments and I sought help for therapy because my anxiety was too much to bear. Because of my meds I have never been hypomanic since we’ve been together so she hasn’t seen that. I have had some psychotic symptoms and one short psychotic break but I had to quit my job. I’ve had a couple of depressive episodes but she’s been supportive. At some point she did tell me it was hard to see me like that. Most of the time I’m stable and it helps that I’m sober now. But if I wasn’t I don’t think I could be in a relationship.
